The next big quick commerce story may not be about groceries

Peeko just raised ₹67.4 crore.

On the surface, it looks like another quick-commerce funding story.

But I think there is something more interesting happening here.

Peeko isn't just trying to deliver baby products faster.

It is trying to become a parenting partner.

That means understanding what parents need, keeping those products available, and making those everyday purchases easier.

From diapers and baby food to toys and kids’ essentials, Peeko has built a catalogue of 30,000+ products, with 60-minute delivery across Bengaluru.

And the early traction is interesting.

More than 1 lakh parents have already used the platform, while revenue has grown nearly 5X since the beginning of 2026.

That tells you something about the opportunity.

Parents don't just need another place to shop.
They need convenience they can rely on, especially when the need is urgent.

And that's where Peeko's business story gets interesting.

It isn't trying to win quick commerce by becoming bigger than everyone else.
It is trying to win by becoming more relevant to one customer.

Because sometimes, the strongest business isn't the one that serves everyone.
It's the one that understands a specific customer so well that switching away feels difficult.

Would you build a bigger platform, or become a brand one audience can’t live without?
comment: The real test will be retention, not just delivery speed. In parenting categories, trust, availability during urgent moments, and habit formation may matter more than adding more SKUs.
